descs.t: Abdul El-Sayed has won the US Senate race in Michigan, defeating Republican Mike Rogers and becoming the first Muslim elected to the US Senate, according to AP. Detroit's count gave him 93% of the vote. We walk through how the race was called and where the votes came from.

Abdul El-Sayed beat Mike Rogers in Michigan's Senate race, and some Michigan Republicans told reporters they voted Democrat this time. An early exit poll of Jewish voters also showed El-Sayed ahead. We look at who crossed over, what El-Sayed said to Trump and Vance, and what this seat means for the Senate.

Michigan just sent Abdul El-Sayed, a progressive Democrat, to the US Senate as its first Muslim member, and he opened by taunting Trump and Vance. We judge him the way we judge everyone: by what his votes will do to your freedom, not by his religion. Plus the fraud claims that flew on election day and what the record shows.

intro.plain: Michigan has called its Senate race. Abdul El-Sayed beat Mike Rogers and becomes the first Muslim elected to the US Senate, according to AP. Detroit gave him 93% of its vote. I want to go through how this happened and where the votes came from. Chat, tell me: did you expect Michigan to go this way?
intro.mid: Abdul El-Sayed has won Michigan, and the story is who voted for him. Some Republicans told reporters they voted Democrat because Rogers was too close to Trump. And El-Sayed's first move was to tell Trump he can just call him Senator. So what kind of senator will he be? Chat, what is the first vote you will be watching him on?
intro.bold: Michigan just elected the first Muslim senator in American history, and the internet lost its mind on both sides. Here is my rule: I do not care about anyone's religion. I care what their votes do to your freedom. El-Sayed opened by taunting Trump and Vance. Now he has to govern. Chat, judge him by the record: what is the one vote that decides it for you?

hook.plain: Abdul El-Sayed has beaten Mike Rogers in Michigan and becomes the first Muslim elected to the US Senate. Here is how the race was won.
hook.mid: Michigan Republicans said on camera they voted Democrat, and Mike Rogers lost. Here is who crossed over and what Abdul El-Sayed does next.
hook.bold: He told Trump to just call him Senator. Michigan's new senator will be judged here the only way that counts: by what his votes do to your freedom.

descs.t: Donald Trump posted a long run of endorsements, backing Vivek Ramaswamy for Governor of Ohio, Byron Donalds for Governor of Florida, Marsha Blackburn for Governor of Tennessee and Brandon Herrera for Texas' 23rd Congressional District, among many others. We go through the list race by race and what each pick means.

Trump endorsed candidates for governor, Senate and the House in Ohio, Florida, Texas, New York, Arizona, Alabama, Michigan and more, calling them America First Patriots. We look at which races he chose to weigh in on and what his backing does for each candidate.

Trump just laid out his slate: Ramaswamy in Ohio, Donalds in Florida, Paxton in Texas, Tuberville in Alabama, Blakeman in New York and dozens more. We break down who made the list, which seats are in play and how much his name still moves Republican voters.

intro.plain: Donald Trump just posted a long string of endorsements. Vivek Ramaswamy for Governor of Ohio, Byron Donalds for Florida, Marsha Blackburn for Tennessee, Brandon Herrera in Texas' 23rd, and many more for the House and Senate. This tells us which races he is putting his name on. So chat, which of these picks do you think matters most?
intro.mid: Trump went on an endorsement spree tonight. Governors, senators, House seats, from Ohio to Alaska to Texas. Ramaswamy, Donalds, Paxton, Tuberville, Blakeman. Every one of them called an America First Patriot. The question is how much his backing still moves voters. Chat, does a Trump endorsement still decide a Republican race in your state?
intro.bold: Trump just drew his map. In one burst he endorsed Ramaswamy for Ohio, Donalds for Florida, Tuberville for Alabama, Paxton in Texas and dozens more, and told Alaska to get out and vote for Dan Sullivan. This is him picking the team he wants around him. Chat, who on this list is the strongest pick, and who is the risk?
